sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2015. Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review: Online appendices. Language 91(3): s1–s188 (supplementary PDF, DOI 10.1353/lan.2015.0049).
sources.note: Nothing about stress. p. s62 (appendix on spurious entries): 'Another three entries are described as extinct Unclassified languages of Colombia with no more precise location given: Coxima [kox], Chipiajes [cbe], Cagua [cbh]. They are not to be found in anywhere else in the literature (except a few recent publication which are derivative of earlier Ethnologue version), including otherwise exhaustive literature on past languages of Colombia (Landaburu 2000, Loukotka 1968, Ortiz 1965). Even if one were to find referent populations for these names, the entries should be removed on the grounds of…

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitter: Editor Ethnologue, SIL International). 2015. Change Request Number 2015-034: Retire [cbh] Cagua (adopted 2016-01-15). 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about stress; it is the retirement form. Rationale (p. 2): 'Alan Wares, in correspondence with Barbara Grimes (5/28/1971), stated that Cagua should be deleted as "non-existent.".. Mention of this language is missing from all the major sources on South American languages (Adelaar 2004, Campbell 1997, Dixon & Aikhenvald 1999, Loukotka 1968, Crevels 2007, Voegelin & Voegelin 1977). Hammarstrom (2015) cites two additional sources (Landaburu 2000, Ortiz 1965) for the non-attestation of Cagua.'

No linguistic data; entry 'has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes.. retired because it was based on a misunderstanding to begin with'; ISO cbh retired 2016 via CR 2015-034 as non-existent; no references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
Nothing; status Deprecated, retired by CR 2015-034 effective 2016-01-15, no successor code.
not reachable by automated download; not read. Per CR 2015-034 the Ethnologue entry had had no information added in ~40 years.
